ai.title: Raise agent step limit to 40 in CLI and evals
ai.summary: Set maxAgentSteps to 40 in cli/src/hooks/use-send-message.ts and evals/buffbench/agent-runner.ts. Extends agent execution budget. Adds mandatory read_files instruction to .agents/base2/base2.ts.

eli5.text: You will notice the assistant can now take a little more time to work through a task before it has to stop and return an answer, instead of giving up after a smaller number of steps. The system quietly let a single setting that limits how long automated runs can stay active bump up to allow more work steps before halting. If you are using the public version of the system today, you should be able to run this yourself and watch the agent continue working past the point where it previously gave up, and automated grading runs used to judge agent performance will also get this longer budget. The change only affects runs that already ask for more time than before, and it is in effect now.

ai.title: Move database and sync utilities to @codebuff/internal
ai.summary: Database access (`db`, `schema`) and sync utilities (`logSyncFailure`) moved from `@codebuff/common` to new `@codebuff/internal` package. Backend files updated to import from internal paths. CI matrix adds `packages/internal` and `packages/billing` for test runs. Prettier formatting applied to agent definitions and CLI scripts.

eli5.text: The CLI's automated assistants got their code reorganized and reformatted. Agent definitions like code-sketcher, file-explorer, planner-pro, and deep-thinker received prettier formatting changes, some lines were reformatted or collapsed into single lines. The CI testing configuration now explicitly includes new packages called 'internal' and 'billing' in its test runs. The backend's agent-run.ts swapped its database imports from '@codebuff/common/db' to '@codebuff/internal/db'. If you opened the assistant definitions, you'd see cleaner line wrapping and spacing; if you used the CLI, you wouldn't notice any functional difference today since these are formatting and import path changes.

ai.title: Standardize env access via @codebuff/common/env
ai.summary: Refactored environment variable access across CLI, backend, and common packages to use a centralized `env` object imported from `@codebuff/common/env` or `@codebuff/internal/env`. This replaces direct `process.env` reads in files like `cli/src/utils/analytics.ts`, `backend/src/index.ts`, and `common/src/analytics.ts`. The change ensures consistent typing, validation, and handling of client vs internal environment variables, reducing reliance on implicit global state.

eli5.text: If you run Codebuff from a terminal, it now reads your secret key and settings from one consistent place instead of hunting through many scattered spots. This prevents the wrong value from sneaking in when it runs locally, behind a proxy, or in CI, and it keeps debug logs and login links working the same way everywhere. You probably won't notice anything different day-to-day, but things like starting the app, signing in, and sending usage stats should behave more reliably across different setups.

ai.title: Revert env schema refactor in CLI and backend
ai.summary: Reverts the centralized `env` schema refactor, restoring direct `process.env` access in CLI and backend modules. Removes `@codebuff/common/env` and `@codebuff/internal/env` imports in favor of raw environment variables. Affects auth, analytics, logging, and login constants.

eli5.text: The CLI and backend stopped using a shared configuration helper for reading secret settings and went back to reading those settings directly from the system, restoring the old login constants and analytics checks. This means environment variables like your API key and PostHog keys are now read the same way they were before the centralized refactor, so nothing should change for you day-to-day, but it rolls back the recent move to a single shared config file. The change is live now and affects anyone using the command-line tool or hitting the backend auth/analytics flows, reverting to the previous direct access pattern.

ai.title: Centralize env vars via @codebuff/common/env
ai.summary: Refactor environment variable access to use typed `env` object from `@codebuff/common/env` and `@codebuff/internal/env` instead of direct `process.env` reads. This change standardizes configuration handling across CLI, backend, and common packages, ensuring consistent validation and type safety. Key files updated include `cli/src/utils/analytics.ts`, `backend/src/util/logger.ts`, and new schema definitions in `common/src/env-schema.ts`.

eli5.text: The program now reads its settings through one central, well-labeled catalog instead of hunting for each value in a big pile of raw system settings, so the backend and the command-line tool stay consistent and are less likely to misread a value. If you ran it today, the behavior is unchanged; the swap only makes future settings easier to add and verify without rewriting every file that uses them.

ai.title: Base2 best-of-n agent pipeline added
ai.summary: Added a new 'best-of-n' mode to the Base2 agent framework, defined in .agents/base2/best-of-n/. This mode spawns multiple 'base2-implementor' agents in parallel to generate code proposals, uses 'base2-selector' to pick the best one, and 'base2-best-of-n-editor' to apply changes. The main 'base2.ts' orchestrator now accepts a 'bestOfN' flag to route tasks through this pipeline instead of direct editing.

eli5.text: The assistant can now take on a more collaborative approach: instead of one agent drafting all the code, it can spawn several independent agents in parallel, each proposing a different way to solve the problem, and then automatically pick the strongest proposal before applying the changes. You would notice this happening through a new option in the Base2 agent framework that, when enabled, routes a coding task through an orchestrator that manages this multi-agent review process rather than editing code directly. This is live today for anyone configuring the Base2 agent with the best-of-N mode, which adds several new specialized roles (the implementors, a selector, and an editor) that coordinate automatically.

ai.title: Refine agent prompts and selector schema
ai.summary: Updated `base2-selector` output schema with descriptions and fixed `implementationId` type. Simplified `base2-implementor` instructions by removing error handling directive. Enhanced `file-researcher` prompt to clarify tool limitations and research-only scope.

eli5.text: The internal AI helpers that draft and review code got their instructions fine-tuned. The one that picks the best draft now explains why it picked it, and the one that writes code was told to skip writing its own error-handling code. The file-finder helper was reminded it can only look things up, not edit anything. You wouldn't notice anything different unless you were peeking at the behind-the-scenes prompt text, so this is the kind of change that tightens things up without changing what you see.

ai.title: Add STEPPROMPT to cache tags, remove assistant heuristic
ai.summary: Updated `convertCbToModelMessages` in `common/src/util/messages.ts` to include `STEP_PROMPT` in the loop applying cache control to preceding messages. Removed the heuristic that tagged the message before the last assistant response, simplifying cache marking to rely on explicit tags. This change affects core message processing for all agents using this utility.

eli5.text: When the app prepares messages to send to an AI, it now also marks step-by-step planning messages to be stored for faster reuse, while stopping its previous habit of guessing which earlier message deserved that same storage. You won't see a new button or option, but the behind-the-scenes message handling that all agents use will rely on these explicit planning markers instead of a rough guess.

You won't see any difference on the page; links, prices, and buttons still work the same. This groups environment variable definitions with their Zod schemas, simplifying imports and ensuring Bun's static analysis correctly identifies individual `process.env` references. The change affects shared core and internal packages, maintaining existing validation logic while improving code organization.

eli5.text: A behind-the-scenes cleanup moved where the app collects its configuration settings, so all the environment variables (like API keys and URLs) are now gathered together with the rules that validate them, then handed off to the parts of the program that need them. If you looked, the settings still behave exactly the same, just stored in one tidy place instead of scattered. This is internal maintenance with no visible change for you today.

eli5.text: The web configuration file for the company's website had a line that loaded environment settings from an internal package, but that line was no longer needed and has been removed. This is purely a behind-the-scenes cleanup that has no visible effect on the website or the people who visit it today.

ai.title: WEBSITEURL now requires NEXTPUBLICCODEBUFFAPPURL
ai.summary: WEBSITE_URL constant in sdk/src/constants.ts no longer falls back to hardcoded localhost or production URLs, relying exclusively on NEXT_PUBLIC_CODEBUFF_APP_URL. scripts/init-worktree.ts updated to inject NEXT_PUBLIC_CODEBUFF_APP_URL into .env.worktree, ensuring dev environments provide the required variable. Scope covers SDK constants and worktree initialization scripts. Missing NEXT_PUBLIC_CODEBUFF_APP_URL results in undefined WEBSITE_URL.

eli5.text: The app now gets its website address from one required setting instead of guessing between a local test address and the real site, and if that setting is missing the address is simply blank. Anyone spinning up a local copy of the system will need that setting provided automatically, otherwise the system won't know where its own website lives. If you were to look at a local setup right now, you'd see the website address pointing to your local port by default instead of falling back to a guessed URL.

ai.title: Fix cache control for single string messages
ai.summary: Refactored `convertCbToModelMessages` in `common/src/util/messages.ts` to correctly apply `cache_control` to single-string messages by iterating backward through content blocks and splitting text parts. The logic now skips short text segments (<2 chars) and ensures the final valid content block receives the ephemeral cache tag. Updated `scripts/fat-sdk-openrouter-example.ts` to demonstrate cache control on system messages with string content.

eli5.text: When you send the assistant a single block of text as a prompt, like a long instruction or request written as plain text instead of formatted chunks, the system now correctly marks that text so the assistant can reuse its response for follow-up questions without re-reading the whole thing. You get faster, cheaper answers on repeat questions because the service can pull from its short-term memory instead of starting over. This fix went live today and affects any plain-text message you send through the system.

ai.title: Update best of n editor to pass through tool results
ai.summary: The best-of-n editor agent now uses structured output mode and a custom `handleSteps` generator to explicitly capture and forward `str_replace` and `write_file` tool results via `set_output`. Previously, the editor relied on `last_message` output mode, which discarded detailed execution feedback. The orchestrator was updated to consume this structured response and tool results array from the spawned editor, ensuring downstream processes receive precise change confirmation data. Changes affect `.agents/base2/best-of-n/base2-best-of-n-editor.ts` and `.agents/base2/best-of-n/base2-best-of-n-orchestrator.ts`.

eli5.text: When the assistant agent makes code edits using its edit and write tools, those tools now report back exactly what changed and confirm each edit was applied successfully, instead of just sending back a rough summary. The coordinator that watches over the agent can now read these detailed confirmations, so it knows precisely which edits were made and can pass that information along to whatever process needs to act on them next. This affects the internal agent system that reviews and applies code changes. If you looked at the system logs, you would see structured feedback showing each successful edit being forwarded, rather than a single vague completion message.

ai.title: SDK 0.5.8 release bundles slash commands, best of N pipeline, and env
ai.summary: The @codebuff/sdk package is bumped to 0.5.8, packaging a release cycle that shipped the /exit and /quit slash commands, the Base2 best-of-n agent pipeline with selector and editor orchestration, and an env variable access refactor across CLI, backend, and web surfaces. Also included are agent step limit increases to 40, write_todos loop behavior changes, login modal hook extractions, and CI env schema generation. The version bump itself reflects accumulated changes rather than introducing new behavior directly in this commit.
ai.evidence: The diff shows a single-line version bump in sdk/package.json from 0.5.7 to 0.5.8. No source code changes are present in this commit; all functional updates are documented in the release notes for the 0.5.8 cycle.

eli5.text: This release introduces a new best-of-N pipeline for the Base2 agent, letting it generate multiple code proposals in parallel and pick the best one automatically for higher-quality results. The CLI now includes a /exit slash command so you can cleanly quit a chat session with /exit, /quit, or /q instead of relying solely on Ctrl+C. A security fix ensures restricted tools can no longer be bypassed during agent runtime, closing a gap that could have allowed unauthorized tool execution. Additionally, the Base2 planner agent now supports step-by-step planning with todos as standard behavior, and message caching has been refined to work correctly with single-string messages and the alloy2 agent. Upgrading gives you more reliable agent planning, cleaner session management, stronger security enforcement, and better handling of cached conversations.
